stem.text: Find the value of \( \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{e^{3x} - 3x - 1}{1 - \cos x + x^{3}} \).

worked_solution.text: As \( x \to 0 \), the numerator \( e^{3x} - 3x - 1 \) tends to \( 0 \).
As \( x \to 0 \), the denominator \( 1 - \cos x + x^{3} \) tends to \( 0 \).

The numerator and the denominator both tend to 0, so the form is \( \frac{0}{0} \) and L'Hospital's rule applies. Differentiate the numerator and the denominator separately: the limit equals \( \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{3e^{3x} - 3}{\sin x + 3x^{2}} \).

The new numerator and denominator both tend to 0 again, so the form is still \( \frac{0}{0} \) and the rule applies once more. Differentiate each separately again: the limit equals \( \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{9e^{3x}}{\cos x + 6x} \).
At \( x = 0 \) this numerator is \( 9 \) and this denominator is \( 1 \), which is not 0, so the limit is \( 9 \).
